records.issue_text: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` is passed straight into `TopicEmbed.import` with no tag/attribute whitelisting. `TopicEmbed.import` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb:10-42`) does no sanitization either — it only rewrites relative URLs via `absolutize_urls` — and stores the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` (`app/models/post.rb:130-137`) short-circuits and returns `raw` unprocessed for `raw_html` posts, bypassing the normal PrettyText/whitelist sanitization pipeline entirely, and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19` renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (explicitly unescaped). A feed item containing `<script>`/`onerror=`/etc. will execute in the context of the forum's own domain for every visitor who views that topic (not just inside the sandboxed iframe embed) — this is a full stored-XSS chain reachable simply by pointing `feed_polling_url` at any feed that isn't fully trusted or that gets compromised.

records.issue_text: `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` uses the open-uri-patched `Kernel#open`, which is a well-known Ruby foot-gun (strings beginning with `|` are executed as a shell pipe). The host-equality check in `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` mitigates the most direct exploitation route today, but it's the only thing standing between untrusted input and `open()`, and it doesn't restrict scheme — `import_remote`'s network fetch happens *before* the `^https?://` check in `TopicEmbed.import` (`topic_embed.rb:11`) is ever reached. Prefer `URI.parse(url).open`/explicit scheme allow-listing before fetching, as defense in depth rather than relying solely on the host-match check.
